text:
Ravi (CS): Heads-up — NovaHealth onboarding hitting sudden 429 bursts after they moved inference calls into short-lived serverless functions. Saw errors spike after a deploy. Need quick triage.

Onboard-Bot: New onboarding ticket #NOV-512 created and linked to this thread. Assigned to Ravi.

Theo (Solutions): thanks. runtime + SDK? are they using provisioned concurrency or pure on-demand?

Ravi (CS): Python SDK v1.8.2 on AWS Lambda (node-style fanout from API GW). Pure on-demand. quick log snippet they pasted: ```[2026-03-21T08:14:02Z] request POST /v1/completions status=429 body="quota exceeded" headers="X-RateLimit-Remaining:0, Retry-After: 3"
[2026-03-21T08:14:02Z] token-refresh start
[2026-03-21T08:14:02Z] token-refresh success
[2026-03-21T08:14:03Z] retrying... backoff=100ms
[2026-03-21T08:14:03Z] request POST /v1/completions status=429
[2026-03-21T08:14:04Z] instance init (cold)
[2026-03-21T08:14:04Z] token-fetch (new)
[2026-03-21T08:14:05Z] flood of requests from same function pid -> many 429s
```

Lina (Eng-Support): looks like a classic cold-start + token-refresh fanout. Lambda cold starts spawn many in-flight requests that each refresh tokens and immediately hammer the API. Two layers to mitigate: prevent simultaneous retries client-side, and reduce cold-start based fanout.

Theo (Solutions): agreed. quick checklist for customer: 1) enable SDK-level token caching across invocations (/tmp on Lambda) so repeated token fetches won't happen on cold starts, 2) add randomized jitter to retry/backoff so retries don't sync, 3) honor Retry-After header and backoff aggressively, 4) consider provisioned concurrency or a small worker pool for high-throughput endpoints.

Ravi (CS): customer can't do provisioned concurrency everywhere. they want minimal changes: allowed to modify function code and env vars.

Lina (Eng-Support): we can ship a small hotfix to Python SDK that: - writes token.json to REDWOOD_TOKEN_CACHE_PATH (default /tmp/redwood-token.json) - uses file lock to avoid stampede - exposes REDWOOD_RESPECT_RETRY_AFTER=true - adds jittered exponential backoff with default max 5 retries. I can prepare a hotfix branch (v1.8.3-lambda-cache).

Theo (Solutions): also recommend they use connection pooling/keep-alive for outbound TLS in the Lambda runtime (reuse client between invocations). Many teams re-instantiate the http client per request which kills keep-alive and increases latency.

Ravi (CS): customer ran an experiment: set concurrency to 2 for their critical route and patched their function to reuse a global SDK client. They saw 95% fewer 429s during a synthetic ramp.

Lina (Eng-Support): good signal. i'll prep the hotfix and a short runbook for customers using serverless: sample code for /tmp token cache, example jittered backoff snippet, and guidance to watch X-RateLimit-Remaining + Retry-After. i'll also add a note about using small warmers if they can't provision concurrency.

Onboard-Bot: Linked PR #sdk-py-1.8.3-lambda-cache created.

Theo (Solutions): for the call with NovaHealth, ask them to: a) confirm function cold-start rate b) show token fetch timestamps c) try the hotfix branch in a canary with low traffic d) capture CloudWatch metrics for downstream 429s.

Ravi (CS): scheduled 30m call with their infra lead tomorrow. i'll push hotfix to them as a package and run canary. will update thread after canary. thanks team :thumbsup:

Lina (Eng-Support): i'll add telemetry in the hotfix to log "token_cache_hit=true/false" so we can quantify stampedes.

Ravi (CS): perfect. marking this triage in progress. will reopen if we still see elevated renewal risk after canary. :white_check_mark:
